summary.headline: KEI Industries Q2 FY27 net sales rose 38.5% to INR 3,776 crores, with EBITDA up 28.7% to INR 401 crores at a 10.62% margin.
summary.overview: Net sales grew 38.5% YoY to INR 3,776 crores and PAT rose 29% to INR 262.45 crores, though PAT margin fell to 6.95% from 7.46%. EBITDA margin was 10.62% against 9.88% last year on the company's operating-margin basis, and the management reiterated its 11% EBITDA margin guidance for the year. Sanand Phase 1 is ramping up, with inventory build of about INR 600-700 crores tied to it. Management said the company has a net cash position, a 25%-plus value growth guidance for FY27 and a 20% CAGR target over 3-4 years.

financial_highlights.change: vs 9.88% prior year (operating margin basis per management)

financial_highlights.metric: Domestic wire and cable sales (Q2 FY27)

segments.name: Wire and cable (total)
segments.commentary: Total wire and cable sales grew 39.5% YoY in Q2 and 32% in H1. Domestic wire and cable grew 38% in H1, while H1 exports were INR 834 crores against INR 846 crores last year.

segments.name: EHV cables
segments.commentary: Q2 EHV sales were INR 217 crores against INR 172 crores, and H1 EHV sales were INR 403 crores against INR 298 crores. Management expects existing EHV capacity at about INR 700 crores of sales, with Sanand adding INR 1,500-1,700 crores of value.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Q2 EPC sales were INR 46 crores against INR 47 crores. Management described the business as being closed down, with a loss of INR 8 crores in Q2 and INR 5 crores in Q1, and expects INR 5-7 crores losses per quarter for one or two more quarters.

segments.name: Stainless steel wire
segments.commentary: Q2 sales were INR 61 crores against INR 53 crores. Capacity utilisation in the stainless steel wire division was 91% in H1.

segments.name: Channel mix
segments.commentary: B2B institutional was 26% of sales, B2C via distribution was 59%, exports 13%, and the balance 2% was domestic EPC and stainless steel wire. Dealer/distributor contribution is in the 55-60% range.

guidance_outlook: FY27 value growth guided at 25%-plus; management said H1 growth of about 30-31% gives room to exceed it.
EBITDA margin guided at about 11% for FY27 on an annualised basis, moving to 11-11.5% and then 11.5-12% as Sanand ramps up, with FY27-28 cited as the timeline for the 11-12% range.
Sustained 20% revenue CAGR targeted for FY28 and the following 3-4 years, funded by working capital and cash flow.

Operating profit targeted to grow 3-4 points above the top line; PAT growth guided at about 3-4 points above top-line growth, and ROE and ROCE expected to return to about 19-20% and 23-24% after Sanand completes.

Sanand Phase 2 EHV and HT cable commercial production is planned by end-March 2027. Sanand sales are targeted at INR 150-200 crores per month in Q3 FY27 and INR 250-300 crores per month in Q3 FY28 (per management); peak Sanand revenue is expected in FY28-29.

Inventory days (about 90 days of COGS) expected to normalise by March 2027. Capex guided at about INR 600 crores a year for 3-4 years, including maintenance capex of INR 100-150 crores (management also cited INR 100-250 crores).
capex_capacity: Total metal-consuming capacity is about 1,83,000 metric tonnes per annum (copper and aluminium). Utilisation in H1 FY27 was 77% in cables, 64% in house wires, 91% in stainless steel wire and 43% in communication cables.
Cumulative capex on Sanand through 30 September 2026 is INR 1,876 crores, with INR 333 crores spent in H1 and about INR 200 crores more expected in H2 FY27. Total H1 capex was INR 402 crores.
CWIP is about INR 1,300 crores as of September, driven mainly by Sanand, and is expected to be capitalised once Phase 2 EHV and HT cable starts by March 2027.
Management expects Sanand EHV ramp-up to take about three months after commissioning for approvals, with sales from the Sanand plant building from the September 2027 quarter.

A new Salarpur project has started and is expected to take about two years to complete. Capex of about INR 600 crores a year is planned for 3-4 years, including growth/infill capex of INR 450-500 crores.
demand_pricing: Export order book is about INR 991 crores, of which roughly 50% is from the USA, with the balance from the Middle East and Australia. Management said the order book converts within 3-4 months.
Order book at the end of September: wire and cable INR 4,927 crores and EPC INR 258 crores.

Pricing is passed through by quoting institutional orders at the prevailing metal price, with a natural hedge from 3-4 months of institutional order book and 3-3.5 months of inventory. Retail prices are revised twice a month.
Management said raw-material price moves pass through and have no effect on margin. It said copper at about 14,800 does not change its volume view, and that volume grows 18-20% if copper stays flat.
Management attributed Q1 vs Q2 margin differences to inventory valuation effects, and said H1 is the right basis for comparison.
Active dealers were 2,146 as of 30 September, against about 2,340 a year earlier. Management said it added more than 25,000 retailers and more than 2 lakh electricians.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Q2 gross margin decline YoY by about 100 bp beyond the EPC loss effect, given prior guidance of margin improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 margin was unrepresentative because of inventory valuation, with the effects averaging out over H1, and that the 11% EBITDA guidance is on an annualised basis. It said H1 operating margin was 11.09% against 10.27-11% over five years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 11% margin guidance a cut from the earlier 11-12% range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no cut: 11% is the FY27 level, moving to 11-11.5% and then 11.5-12% as Sanand ramps up, with the 11-12% range completing across FY27-28.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q2 revenue growth stronger than the usual 20-25% range, and does this imply a slower H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it guides to 25%-plus conservatively to avoid missing guidance. It said H1 growth of about 30-31% already exceeds that guidance, and that the company will add more growth where capital allows.

qa_highlights.question: Can exports and the US order book support growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export sales were flat at INR 493 crores (vs INR 472 crores), and the export order book is INR 991 crores with the USA at about 50%. It expects export growth to pick up in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the rise in inventory and working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said more than INR 600-700 crores of the inventory build is at Sanand, with the balance from copper valuation at the existing plants. It expects inventory to normalise to about 90 days of COGS by March 2027, and said debtor days have already fallen.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EHV revenue opportunity after Sanand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Sanand adds INR 1,500-1,700 crores of new EHV capacity in value terms on top of existing EHV sales of about INR 700 crores, with peak Sanand revenue in FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: How much of growth is volume versus value, and what is the capital constraint?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is guided in value terms because budgets are set in value and working capital limits growth to about 25-30%. It said a 16-17% volume growth with 50% price growth would imply a 67-70% value increase, which it considers unfeasible.

risks_watch: Gross and EBITDA margin: Q2 EBITDA margin of 10.62% is below the 11% full-year guide, and the Q1/Q2 split depends on inventory-valuation timing.
Working capital and cash flow: inventory build of about INR 1,200 crores in H1 and the working capital ramp-up at Sanand, with normalisation expected only by March 2027.
Sanand ramp-up pace: Q3 FY27 monthly sales of INR 250-300 crores (per management) and peak utilisation targeted for FY28-29.
Competition from new entrants (including Ultravolt), which management says will not trigger pricing wars, and its impact on dealer and institutional share.
Export order conversion and geopolitical exposure: the order book has a 3-4 month life, and management said export growth depends on geopolitics and competition.
Copper price moves above 15,000 and their effect on demand, and the EPC closure's impact on PAT (about INR 5-7 crores per quarter loss for one or two more quarters).
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the 25%-plus growth guidance, but defensive and repetitive on margin, with the 11% guidance clarified as annualised and restated several times. Management avoided volume-number questions and deflected questions on the exact guide with value-growth framing.
key_quotes: So we should not compare as we earlier requested for Q1 or Q2, it is an annualized basis.
Once the Sanand is fixed and the capacity is ramping up and we are going to utilize to 60% to 70%, our EBITDA margin will definitely cross to 11%.
Because we need to increase the capacity to grow by 20% CAGR. So now we have just started the Salarpur.

So whatever guidance this year, we have upgraded to grow by 25%, so we are still maintaining that we will grow more than 25% because nobody knows that in future copper price will go up or copper price will go down.
So 70% which is not possible at all because for growing any company, it needs the working capital and working capital does not support more than 25% to 30% growth rate.
